messages:
elaine: Heads-up — ACME reported large p95/p99 increase since ~2200 UTC last night, they see long tails and occasional 503s. They say overall throughput is fine but some requests take 5-20s. :frowning:
raj: saw spike in GPU memory usage on the serving pool for region-us-east-1 around the same time. Memory headroom dropped and kernels started hitting the slower allocator path. :eyes:
ben: dumping a short timeline now. infra-bot, can you attach the last 2h GPU mem heatmap for pool r-e1?
infra-bot: Attached heatmap: /artifacts/gpu-heatmaps/r-e1/174555-2h.png
tina: quick checks — no deploys logged after 21:45 UTC, autoscaler steady. Customer workload looks like a higher fraction of long-context chat requests (>4096 tokens) starting 22:10.
elaine: ACME says they didn't change prompts. Could be model switching or a routing fallback to a quantized variant that increases KV churn.
raj: looking at allocator metrics: slab_free_ratio fell from 0.32 to 0.06. Fragmentation metric (slab_entropy) up 4x. KV cache entries also jumped ~3x for that tenant group.
ben: paste of the hot logs:
```
2024-11-09T22:12:11Z runtime WARN slab: unable to satisfy 128MB alloc (largest_free 96MB) -> falling back to freelist slow path
2024-11-09T22:12:11Z runtime INFO kvcache: insert tenant=acme size=86MB total_kv=1.4GB
2024-11-09T22:12:12Z runtime ERROR request: p95 spike route=/v1/chat model=redwood-large-16k
```
raj: repro plan: replicate with a replay that mixes long-concat chats at scale, and enable per-tenant kv_bloom debug to track churn.
elaine: for immediate mitigation can we (1) throttle ACME by 10% request rate, (2) enable slab-compact for pool r-e1 on a rolling basis, (3) evict oldest KV entries for tenants over 1GB.
ben: I can trigger a slab-compact shim that runs a conservative compaction across GPUs; it takes ~40s per GPU and causes small CPU spike. Rolling across pool should keep p99 stable.
tina: alternative quick fix: change routing for ACME to the warm fallback variant (redwood-medium-8k) — halves KV memory use. Might change output quality though.
raj: also adding an allocator param tweak: increase per-arena coalesce threshold from 32MB->64MB to reduce freelist fragmentation. I'll stage on canary now.
elaine: please include exact commands in the thread so support can tell customer what to expect.
ben: commands I ran:
```
# start conservative slab compaction on pool r-e1
infractl runtime slab-compact --pool r-e1 --mode rolling --parallel 1
# evict per-tenant KV over threshold
infractl kv evict --tenant acme --threshold 1GB --policy lru
# route tenant to medium variant
infractl route set --tenant acme --model redwood-medium-8k --weight 1.0
```
raj: canary allocator tweak:
```
# apply allocator coalesce param on node group r-e1-canary
infractl node update --group r-e1-canary --set allocator.coalesce_threshold=64MB
```
infra-bot: Canaries applied to r-e1-canary at 1745556840. Monitoring.
ben: after running compaction + kv-evict I see mem headroom recover from 6% -> 28% in ~6 minutes; p95 dropped back to baseline in our synthetic replay.
tina: noting for postmortem: root cause probable mix of increased long-context requests + KV retention policy that allowed a tenant to grow KV set unchecked; fragmentation amplified by allocator heuristics.
elaine: action items:
- raj: roll allocator tweak to pool if canary stable (monitor 30m)
- ben: document slab-compact runbook and safe parameters
- tina: talk to customer success about temporary rate-limit + routing change and confirm acceptance
- infra-bot: attach link to monitoring dashboards + replay artifacts
infra-bot: dashboards: https://grafana.internal/r/e1-memory; replay artifacts: /replays/174555-acme-longctx.tar.gz
raj: will update here in 30m with canary verdict. :thumbsup:
elaine: thanks team, keeping ACME updated. If p99 resurfaces escalate to oncall with trace ids.
